citations.quote:
Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ of type
$A_{n-1}$ with Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system $\Phi^+$, Weyl vector
$\rho$, Weyl group $W$ (identified with $S_n$) and dot action
$w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$. Fix a dominant regular integral weight
$\lambda$, i.e. $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\neq0$ for every root and
$\lambda$ integral, and let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be the corresponding regular
integral block in the conventions of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]: standard
objects $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)=M(w\cdot\lambda)$, simples $L(w\cdot\lambda)$,
indecomposable projectives $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\in W$, with
$\lambda=e\cdot\lambda$ the unique dominant and $w_0\cdot\lambda$ the unique
antidominant element and $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$.

This item freezes the following conventions, each inherited from the cited
suppliers and used verbatim below.

(i) **Multiplicity conventions.** $(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))$ is
the Verma-flag multiplicity of [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] and
$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$ the composition multiplicity, and
$$(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$$
by BGG reciprocity ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]).

(ii) **Bruhat reversal convention.** Along the bijection
$W\ni w\mapsto w\cdot\lambda$ the Bruhat order runs opposite to the dominance
order, in the two exact senses used on this page: $y\le w$ implies
$w\cdot\lambda\le y\cdot\lambda$ in the dominance order, and every nonzero
multiplicity forces the index direction, i.e.
$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]\neq0$ implies $y\le w$ in the Bruhat
order. The first sense is the inclusion direction of
[[lem-dominant-integral-dot-translates-embed-in-the-verma-module]] (for
$w\ge y$ one has $M(w\cdot\lambda)\subseteq M(y\cdot\lambda)$, so the highest
weight of the submodule is the lower one), and the second is
[[lem-jordan-holder-factors-of-verma-modules-lie-above-the-head]], which
confines every composition factor of $M(y\cdot\lambda)$ to labels
$w\ge y$. The full statement that the two orders are isomorphic as posets is
not needed here and is not asserted; only these two directions, together with
the finiteness of intervals of the Bruhat order
([[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]), are used.

(iii) **Hecke and Kazhdan–Lusztig normalization.** The Kazhdan–Lusztig basis
$\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ of the normalized type-$A$ Hecke
algebra ([[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]), with
$$p_{y,w}=v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(v^{-2})$$
in the classical $q=v^{-2}$ normalization
([[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]), support
$p_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, diagonal $p_{w,w}=1$, and simultaneous inversion
symmetry $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$.

(iv) **Soergel label and character dictionary.** Write $R_x$ for the
polynomial standard graph bimodule supported at $x$, and $B_x$ for the
normalized indecomposable polynomial Soergel bimodule, which is generally not a
standard graph bimodule. With right reduction $\bar B=B\otimes_S\mathbb C$
and left coinvariant-module values of $V$, the projective dictionary is
$$V(P(w\cdot\lambda))\cong\bar B_{w^{-1}}$$
([[thm-indecomposable-projectives-correspond-to-indecomposable-soergel-modules]]).
The graph label $x$ corresponds to the standard
$\Delta(x^{-1}\cdot\lambda)$. The individual support ranks are measured on the
polynomial lift before reduction, as in
[[prop-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-standard-filtration-ranks-under-v]];
no separated graph-support filtration of the reduced module is asserted.

For degree bookkeeping use precisely the standard-generator normalization of
[[def-type-a-standard-graph-bimodules-support-filtrations-and-character]]:
$\Delta_x(d)=R_x(d-\ell(x))$, and $r_{x,d}(B)$ counts these normalized polynomial
standard layers. Thus the coefficient polynomial is
$$m_x(B;v):=\sum_d r_{x,d}(B)v^d,\qquad h_\Delta(B)=\sum_xm_x(B;v)\widetilde T_x,\qquad\widetilde T_x=v^{\ell(x)}T_x.$$
Here $\widetilde T_x$ is the normalized **standard** Hecke element $H_x$ used
in clause (iii) and
[[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]]. The published
Soergel split-Grothendieck-ring convention instead names its simple
Kazhdan--Lusztig generators $H_i=v(T_i+1)=\widetilde T_{s_i}+v$; these must not
be confused with the standard element $H_{s_i}=vT_i$
([[thm-split-grothendieck-group-of-the-soergel-category-is-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]]).
The standard-character supplier
[[lem-the-type-a-standard-character-is-multiplicative]] identifies $h_\Delta$
with that split-Grothendieck-ring isomorphism. This records the coefficient
normalization, and does not infer the image of a general indecomposable $B_x$
by multiplying simple generators. In particular the character theorem must be
used to identify $h_\Delta(B_x)$ with $\underline H_x$; a product of simple
Soergel classes is a Bott--Samelson class and need not be $[B_x]$.
The inverse labels and all rank comparisons above use auxiliary polynomial
gradings only; forgetting them gives the ordinary projective dictionary.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If a projective object
$P$ of $\mathcal O$ admits an epimorphism $P\twoheadrightarrow L$ onto a
simple object $L$, then some indecomposable direct summand of $P$ maps onto
$L$, and that summand is a projective cover of $L$ (an essential epimorphism
with projective source, [[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]]).
Any two projective covers of $L$ are isomorphic, although not canonically so,
and the endomorphism ring of a projective cover is local. In particular, for
every simple $L$ there is at most one isomorphism class of indecomposable
projectives with head $L$; when such a cover exists it is written $P(L)$.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category in which every object has finite
length, and define an object to be **indecomposable** when it is nonzero and
every decomposition $X\cong Y\oplus Z$ has $Y=0$ or $Z=0$. Then:

1. every object of $\mathcal A$ is a finite direct sum of indecomposable
   objects;
2. the endomorphism ring of an indecomposable object is local, and for an
   endomorphism $f$ of an indecomposable object either $f$ is an isomorphism
   or $f$ is nilpotent;
3. the decomposition is unique up to isomorphism and permutation of the
   summands;
4. an indecomposable projective object $P$ of $\mathcal A$ has a unique
   maximal proper subobject $J(P)$, its quotient $P/J(P)$ is simple, and $P$
   is a projective cover of $P/J(P)$
   ([[def-projective-object]], [[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]];
   projectivity here is relative to $\mathcal A$. In a full subcategory closed
   under submodules, essentiality is the superfluous-kernel condition of the
   cited module definition; projectivity in the ambient module category is
   not asserted).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in category
$\mathcal O$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]], and write
$\Delta(\mu)=M(\mu)$ for the standard objects of
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], i.e. the Verma modules
of [[def-verma-module]].

A **finite Verma flag** of an object $X$ of $\mathcal O$ — also called a
**standard flag** or a **$\Delta$-flag** — is a finite increasing sequence of
subobjects
$$0=X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_n=X$$
such that each quotient $X_i/X_{i-1}$ is isomorphic to a Verma module
$\Delta(\mu_i)=M(\mu_i)$, for $i=1,\dots,n$. An object admitting such a flag is
called **Verma-filtered**. Since the flag is exhausted by its factors, its
class in the Grothendieck group
$K_0(\mathcal O)$ of [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]
is
$$[X]=\sum_{i=1}^n[\Delta(\mu_i)].$$

For a Verma-filtered object $X$ and a weight $\mu$, the **multiplicity**
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is the number of indices $i$ with $\mu_i=\mu$ in a Verma
flag of $X$. This number is independent of the chosen flag by
[[lem-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-independent-of-the-flag]], so the notation
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is well-defined for Verma-filtered $X$.

The zero object has the empty flag, and every multiplicity of the zero object
is zero; a nonzero Verma-filtered object has at least one factor. A one-step
flag of $X$ is exactly an isomorphism $X\cong\Delta(\mu)$ for a single weight
$\mu$, so the objects with a one-step flag are the Verma modules themselves.
The flag is a chain of subobjects of $X$ in the module category; it is not
required to split, and later examples show that it need not.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and work in a regular integral type-A block over
$\mathbb C$. With the page's right wall-crossing convention and left
$C$-module values of $V$, there is an equivalence
$$V\colon\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal O_\lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{\text{ungraded Soergel modules }B\otimes_S\mathbb C\},\qquad P(w\cdot\lambda)\longmapsto\bar B_{w^{-1}}.$$
The target is the additive category of direct summands of the right reductions
of polynomial Bott-Samelson bimodules, or equivalently of iterated
$C\otimes_{C^s}(-)$ applied to the trivial module $\mathbb C$, not to the
regular module $C$. For $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, the projective is the unique new
top-label summand of $\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)$; applying
$V$ gives the new summand of $\overline{B_{s_k}\cdots B_{s_1}}$, thus the
inverse label. These normalized indecomposable polynomial lifts supply
self-dual auxiliary gradings; in rank one the centered degrees are $-1,1$,
with degrees $0,2$ after an uncentered shift. Forgetting grading recovers the
projective dictionary. More generally the ungraded equivalence with
Weyl-group Soergel modules holds for every complex semisimple regular integral
block; the type-A diagrammatic label comparison applies only in type A.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a projective $P$ in a regular integral type-A
block, choose its polynomial Soergel lift $\mathsf B(P)$ determined by the
preceding projective dictionary: if $P=\bigoplus_wP(w\cdot\lambda)^{m_w}$, take
$\mathsf B(P)=\bigoplus_wB_{w^{-1}}^{m_w}$, so that its right reduction is
$V(P)$ after forgetting auxiliary grading. Write $r_{x,d}(\mathsf B(P))$ for
the graded multiplicity of the polynomial standard graph module supported at
$x$ in its standard support filtration, with the standard-generator
normalization of the polynomial Soergel category. Then
$$(P:\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_d r_{y^{-1},d}(\mathsf B(P)).$$
Equivalently the polynomial Soergel character of this lift, evaluated at $v=1$
and with inverse labels, recovers the ordinary Verma-flag character of $P$.
These are ranks before reduction; no separated Bruhat-support filtration
intrinsic to the finite-dimensional module $V(P)$ is asserted, since the graph
supports coalesce at the origin. The same ungraded multiplicity comparison
holds with the corresponding Weyl-group polynomial/deformed lifts in other
complex semisimple types.

derivations.claim: The object $P:=P(w\cdot\lambda)$ is a nonzero indecomposable projective of $\mathcal O_\lambda$, namely a projective cover of the simple $L(w\cdot\lambda)$, and by the projective dictionary [F2] its Soergel value is $V(P)=\bar B_{w^{-1}}$, the right reduction of the single polynomial lift $B_{w^{-1}}$.

Every decomposition of $P$ into indecomposables is a one-summand decomposition. Indeed, by [F5] a decomposition $P\cong\bigoplus_v P(v\cdot\lambda)^{m_v}$ exists and any two such decompositions agree up to isomorphism and permutation of summands; since the nonzero object $P$ is an indecomposable projective cover by [F4], only one summand can be present, so the decomposition is $P\cong P(v\cdot\lambda)$ for a single label $v$. Applying the equivalence $V$ of [F2] to this isomorphism gives $\bar B_{w^{-1}}\cong\bar B_{v^{-1}}$; as $V$ is a bijection on isomorphism classes of indecomposables, $v=w$. Hence in the dictionary of [F3] the polynomial lift assigned to $P$ is the single term $\mathsf B(P)=B_{w^{-1}}$, with no further summands.

Substitute $\mathsf B(P)=B_{w^{-1}}$ from step 1.2 into the general rank comparison [F3] applied to the projective $P=P(w\cdot\lambda)$: its left side is the Verma-flag multiplicity $(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))$ of [F1] and [F6], and its right side is $\sum_d r_{y^{-1},d}(B_{w^{-1}})$, the sum of the graded standard-support multiplicities of the polynomial lift $B_{w^{-1}}$. This is the displayed identity for all $y,w\in W$. The ranks on the right are pre-reduction ranks of the polynomial lift, by the final clause of [F3] and by the reduction convention [F2]; no separated filtration of $V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$ is produced or used.

boundaries.evidence: Step 2.1 concludes that the decomposition of P(w.lambda) into indecomposables has a single summand; the empty summand case is excluded because P(w.lambda) is a nonzero projective cover in step 1.1.

The Statement is an identity of integers for every pair (y,w) in W x W; in step 2.1 both sides instantiate the same multiplicity, so pairs whose flag multiplicity vanishes are asserted by the identity rather than excluded from it.
The diagonal case y = w and the single-summand lift B_{w^{-1}} are both inside the Statement's quantifier; step 2.1 applies the rank comparison to that one-summand projective.

boundaries.reason: The Lemma is confined to a regular integral type-A block. Non-integral parameters and singular central characters lie outside the hypotheses of the cited rank comparison and block theory, and are not claimed.

boundaries.evidence: The extremal labels y = w_0 and w = w_0 are covered by the universal quantifier; step 2.1's substitution x = y^{-1} applies at the antidominant label exactly as elsewhere.
The Statement assumes AC; step 2.1 consumes the inherited choice only through the projective-cover and Krull-Schmidt theory of [F4] and [F5], the sole selection step in the proof.

boundaries.reason: The Lemma asserts a single equality of multiplicities, not a biconditional; there is no forward implication to discharge beyond the equality itself.
No reverse implication is claimed: the Lemma does not assert that sums of graded standard ranks can be read back from an arbitrary multiplicity table outside the stated block.

citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be a regular integral
type-$A$ block with $W=S_n$, and for $w\in W$ let $B_{w^{-1}}$ be the polynomial
Soergel lift of $V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$, so that
$V(P(w\cdot\lambda))=\bar B_{w^{-1}}$ is its right reduction. Write
$r_{x,d}(B)$ for the graded multiplicity of the polynomial standard graph
module supported at $x$ in the standard support filtration of a polynomial
Soergel bimodule $B$, in the standard-generator normalization of the polynomial
Soergel category. Then for all $y,w\in W$
$$(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_d r_{y^{-1},d}(B_{w^{-1}}).$$
These are ranks before reduction: the right side sums the graded standard
support multiplicities of the polynomial lift, not multiplicities in any
separated filtration of the finite-dimensional module $V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$.

**Graphs and supports.** Keep $k=\mathbb Q$, $R=\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with
$\deg x_i=2$, and the affine scheme $V=\mathbb A^n_k=\operatorname{Spec}R$,
whose $k$-points are $V(k)=k^n$. Use the place-permuting action of $S_n$
from [[def-type-a-reflection-realization-and-polynomial-ring]].
For $w\in S_n$ let
$$Gr(w):=\operatorname{Graph}(w:V\to V)\subseteq V\times_kV,\quad Gr(w)(k)=\{(w\lambda,\lambda):\lambda\in k^n\},\qquad Gr(A):=\bigcup_{w\in A}Gr(w)\ \ (A\subseteq S_n),$$
so that $V\times_kV=\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kR)$ and $Gr(w)$ is the graph
of the map $\lambda\mapsto w\lambda$. A graded $(R,R)$-bimodule $M$ is the
same thing as a graded module over $R\otimes_kR$, and the support of $m\in M$ is
the zero set $\operatorname{supp}(m):=V(\operatorname{Ann}(m))\subseteq V\times V$
of its annihilator ideal in $R\otimes_kR$. For $A\subseteq S_n$ put
$$\Gamma_AM:=\{m\in M:\operatorname{supp}(m)\subseteq Gr(A)\},$$
a graded sub-bimodule of $M$. Since $Gr(A)$ is closed with radical ideal
$I(Gr(A))=\bigcap_{w\in A}I(Gr(w))$ (an intersection of prime ideals, since each
$Gr(w)$ is a linear subspace of $V\times V$ complementing the second factor), an
element $m$ lies in $\Gamma_AM$ exactly when $I(Gr(A))^N m=0$ for some $N\ge0$:
this is the Nullstellensatz together with the Noetherianity of
$R\otimes_kR$. The ideal itself need not annihilate such an element — in
$(R\otimes_kR)/I(Gr(e))^2$ the class of $1$ is supported on $Gr(e)$ but is not
killed by $I(Gr(e))$ — which is why the criterion is stated with a power of the
ideal. For $i\in\mathbb Z$ we write
$$\Gamma_{\ge i}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\ell(x)\ge i\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{\le i}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\ell(x)\le i\}}M,$$
using the length function of [[lem-type-a-reduced-words-are-connected-by-braid-moves]],
while for $y\in S_n$ the $y$-indexed symbols denote the *Bruhat
principal-set* cutoffs of Soergel's Notation 6.1,
$$\Gamma_{\le y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x\le y\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{<y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x<y\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{\ge y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x\ge y\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{>y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x>y\}}M,$$
with $\Gamma_yM:=\Gamma_{\{y\}}M$ the elements concentrated on the single graph
$Gr(y)$ and $\Gamma_{\ne y}M:=\Gamma_{S_n\setminus\{y\}}M$ the elements
concentrated off $Gr(y)$. The integer-indexed symbols of the previous display are
the *length* cutoffs used to define the flags below, and they must not be
confused with the element-indexed Bruhat cutoffs: for $y=s_1$ in $S_4$ the
submodule $\Gamma_{\le1}M$ contains $Gr(s_3)$ while
$\Gamma_{\le y}M=\Gamma_{\{e,s_1\}}M$ does not, and the two cutoffs agree at
the extremes, $\Gamma_{\le w_0}=\Gamma_{\le\ell(w_0)}=M$ and
$\Gamma_{<e}=\Gamma_{\le-1}=0$. So
$\Gamma^yM:=M/\Gamma_{\ne y}M$ is Soergel's $y$-layer
*quotient*; following Soergel's
Notation 6.1 we write the two $y$-layer quotients with an underline,
$$\underline{\Gamma}_{\le y}M:=\Gamma_{\le y}M/\Gamma_{<y}M,\qquad \underline{\Gamma}_{\ge y}M:=\Gamma_{\ge y}M/\Gamma_{>y}M,$$
so that $\underline{\Gamma}_{\le y}M$ is the quotient of the lower support
submodule by $\Gamma_{<y}M$ and $\underline{\Gamma}_{\ge y}M$ the quotient of
the upper support submodule by the part supported strictly above $Gr(y)$.

**Standard bimodules.** For $w\in S_n$ let $R_w$ be the graded $(R,R)$-bimodule
which equals $R$ as a graded $k$-vector space and has
$$f\cdot x=fx,\qquad x\cdot g=w(g)\,x\qquad(f,g,x\in R),$$
where $w(g)(\lambda):=g(w^{-1}\lambda)$; $R_w$ is generated by the element $1$ of
degree $0$. Write $(k)$ for the *external* shift $M(k):=M\{-k\}$ of
[[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]], so that
$M(k)_d=M_{d+k}$; this is the shift convention of the type-A sources, and it is
the one in which $B_i=R\otimes_{R^{s_i}}R(1)$ of
[[def-type-a-soergel-bimodule-for-a-simple-reflection]] has $1\otimes1$ of
degree $-1$. Put
$$\Delta_w(d):=R_w(d-\ell(w)),\qquad \nabla_w(d):=R_w(d+\ell(w))\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$
so that $\Delta_w(d)$ is the standard bimodule $R_w$ with its generator in
degree $\ell(w)-d$, and $\nabla_w(d)$ is $R_w$ with its generator in degree
$-\ell(w)-d$. Thus $\Delta_w(0)=R_w\{\ell(w)\}$,
$\nabla_w(0)=R_w\{-\ell(w)\}$ and $\Delta_e(d)=\nabla_e(d)=R(d)$ is generated
in degree $-d$; in particular $\Delta_e(0)=\nabla_e(0)=R_e=R$.

For graded free $R$-modules in this type-A page, a homogeneous free generator of degree $a$ contributes $v^a$ to graded rank. This is the $v\mapsto v^{-1}$ transform of Soergel's rank convention in his Notation 5.2; all rank formulas below use this convention.

**Support filtrations.** A $\Delta$-flag of a graded $R$-bimodule $M$ is a
finite chain $0=M_0\subseteq M_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_k=M$ of graded
sub-bimodules which refines the length filtration
$$M=\Gamma_{\ge0}M\supseteq\Gamma_{\ge1}M\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\Gamma_{\ge\ell(w_0)+1}M=0$$
of $M$ (here $\Gamma_{\ge0}M=M$ for every bimodule supported on
$Gr(S_n)=\bigcup_{w}Gr(w)$, which all bimodules of this page are, and
$\Gamma_{\ge i}M=0$ for $i>\ell(w_0)$ because no graph $Gr(x)$ with
$\ell(x)>i$ remains) and whose successive quotients are
standard bimodules $M_j/M_{j-1}\cong R_{x_j}\{a_j\}$. We require each
length layer to be a finite direct sum of shifted graph bimodules of that
length, as in Soergel's Definition 5.4. Thus the
quotients carry a numbering with $\ell(x_1)\ge\cdots\ge\ell(x_k)$ and each
$R_{x_j}\{a_j\}$ is one graph, so that $M$ has a "support flag" in the sense of
Soergel's $F_\Delta$. A $\nabla$-flag has the same direct-sum condition on its length layers, with the reverse length
filtration $\Gamma_{\le i}M$ and $\ell(x_1)\le\cdots\le\ell(x_k)$. The
refinement condition is a condition on supports, not an ordering of incomparable
quotients of equal length; only the lengths are ordered. For $i=\ell(x)$ the
graded multiplicity is
$$(M:\Delta_x(d)):=\text{multiplicity of }\Delta_x(d)\text{ in } \Gamma_{\ge i}M/\Gamma_{\ge i+1}M,$$
and, for a $\nabla$-flag, $(M:\nabla_x(d))$ is the multiplicity of
$\nabla_x(d)$ in $\Gamma_{\le i}M/\Gamma_{\le i-1}M$; a priori both symbols
refer to a chosen compatible enumeration (the next items on this page prove that
they do not depend on it). With $T_x$ the Hecke basis of
[[lem-type-a-hecke-standard-basis-for-soergel-comparison]] and
$\widetilde T_x:=v^{\ell(x)}T_x$, the character sums attached to a flag are
$$h_\Delta(M):=\sum_{x,d}(M:\Delta_x(d))\,v^d\,\widetilde T_x,\qquad h_\nabla(M):=\sum_{x,d}(M:\nabla_x(d))\,v^{-d}\,\widetilde T_x,$$
and they are used only through the items that prove these sums intrinsic.

**Small $n$.** For $n\le1$ there is a single element $e$ and every object is a finite direct sum of shifts $\bigoplus_j R(d_j)$. Its one-graph flags have these summands as quotients, so $h_\Delta=\sum_jv^{d_j}\widetilde T_e$ and $h_\nabla=\sum_jv^{-d_j}\widetilde T_e$; in particular both characters send the unit $R$ to $1$.

For every $w\in S_n$ the character of the indecomposable type-$A$ Soergel bimodule equals the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis element: $\operatorname{ch}(B_w^R)=\underline H_w$. Equivalently, the class $[B_w^R]$ in the split Grothendieck group corresponds to $\underline H_w$ under the Hecke algebra isomorphism, and the extension of scalars of the rational $B_w$ categorifies the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis. Moreover the hard Lefschetz property $\mathrm hL(w)$ and the Hodge-Riemann relations $\mathrm{HR}(w)$ hold for every $w$, with the standard signs, and the same identities hold for the rational category by the base-change comparison. Finally, for every right descent $xs<x$ the matrix of $L_\zeta$ on $B_xB_s=B_x(1)\oplus B_x(-1)$ is $\begin{pmatrix}\rho\cdot(-)&0\\ \zeta\rho(\alpha_s^\vee)&\rho\cdot(-)\end{pmatrix}$; for $\zeta>0$, $\mathrm hL(x)$ implies $\mathrm hL(x,s)_\zeta$ without any additional character hypothesis, since $\mathrm S$ is now established for all elements, while at $\zeta=0$ centered hard Lefschetz fails.

**Graphs and supports.** Keep $k=\mathbb Q$, $R=\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with
$\deg x_i=2$, and the affine scheme $V=\mathbb A^n_k=\operatorname{Spec}R$,
whose $k$-points are $V(k)=k^n$. Use the place-permuting action of $S_n$
from [[def-type-a-reflection-realization-and-polynomial-ring]].
For $w\in S_n$ let

so that $V\times_kV=\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kR)$ and $Gr(w)$ is the graph
of the map $\lambda\mapsto w\lambda$. A graded $(R,R)$-bimodule $M$ is the
same thing as a graded module over $R\otimes_kR$, and the support of $m\in M$ is
the zero set $\operatorname{supp}(m):=V(\operatorname{Ann}(m))\subseteq V\times V$
of its annihilator ideal in $R\otimes_kR$. For $A\subseteq S_n$ put
$$\Gamma_AM:=\{m\in M:\operatorname{supp}(m)\subseteq Gr(A)\},$$
a graded sub-bimodule of $M$. Since $Gr(A)$ is closed with radical ideal
$I(Gr(A))=\bigcap_{w\in A}I(Gr(w))$ (an intersection of prime ideals, since each

element $m$ lies in $\Gamma_AM$ exactly when $I(Gr(A))^N m=0$ for some $N\ge0$:

Let $n\ge1$ and $y,w\in S_n$. The **Bruhat interval** $[y,w]:=\{z\in S_n:y\le z\le w\}$ is finite, with Bruhat order as in [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]] and [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]]. The rank-order definition uses the zero-based model of $S_n$, while $H_v(n)$ uses the one-based model; throughout, identify them by the order-preserving shift $i\mapsto i+1$ on inputs and values.

The **$R$-coefficients** $r_{y,w}\in A=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ are the unique coefficients in the standard-basis expansion
$$\overline{H_w}=H_{w^{-1}}^{-1}=\sum_{y\in S_n}r_{y,w}H_y,$$
where the bar is the involution from [[lem-the-hecke-bar-involution-is-well-defined]] and $\{H_y:y\in S_n\}$ is the standard basis of [[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]]. The sum has finite support because $S_n$ is finite. In rank one, $\overline{H_{s_i}}=H_{s_i}^{-1}=H_{s_i}+(v-v^{-1})H_{\mathrm{id}}$, so $r_{\mathrm{id},s_i}=v-v^{-1}$.

The support, diagonal, and parity properties of these coefficients are stated and proved in [[thm-r-polynomial-recursion-and-degree-bounds]]. This page uses the coefficient normalization given by the displayed bar expansion.

Its reduced subwords give: $1234$ at length $0$; $2134,1324,1243$ at length $1$; $1342,1423,2314,3124,2143$ at length $2$; $1432,2413,3142,3214$ at length $3$; and $3412$ at length $4$. The four elements $1234,2134,1243,2143$ contain no reduced subword equal to $s_2=1324$, so they are not above $b$ by the reduced-subword criterion; the remaining ten elements are exactly $[b,w]$.

**All gaps at most two have $P=1$.** Suppose $y<z$ and $d:=\ell(z)-\ell(y)\le2$. By [F3] the degree of $P_{y,z}$ is at most $(d-1)/2\le1/2$, hence at most $0$; together with constant term $1$ this forces $P_{y,z}=1$. If $d=0$ then $y=z$ and $P_{y,y}=1$; if $y$ and $z$ are incomparable, $P_{y,z}=0$ by [F3]. In particular $P_{b,2413}=1$ and $P_{1234,1423}=1$, both pairs having gap $2$.

With $s=s_1$ one has $s\,2413=1423$ and $s\,\mathrm{id}=2134$, so $c=0$ in [F4] and $$P_{\mathrm{id},2413}(q)=q\,P_{2134,1423}(q)+P_{\mathrm{id},1423}(q)-\!\!\!\sum_{\substack{\mathrm{id}\le u\le1423\\ s_1u<u,\ \mu(u,1423)\ne0}}\!\!\!\mu(u,1423)\,q^{(3-\ell(u))/2}P_{\mathrm{id},u}(q).$$ The first summand vanishes: $1423=s_3s_2$ has no reduced subword $s_1$, so $2134\not\le1423$ and $P_{2134,1423}=0$ by [F3] and [F5]. The correction sum is empty as well: $[\mathrm{id},1423]=\{1234,1324,1243,1423\}$ by step 1.1, and for each of these four elements left multiplication by $s_1$ swaps the values $1$ and $2$, raising the length from $0,1,1,2$ to $1,2,2,3$ respectively, so no element of the interval has the required left descent $s_1$. By step 1.2 the remaining term is $P_{\mathrm{id},1423}=1$, hence $P_{\mathrm{id},2413}=1$.

**The main recursion.** Apply [F4] to $b=1324$, $w=3412$ and the left descent $s=s_2$: $s_2w=2413$ and $s_2b=1234$, so $c=1$ because $s_2b$ has length $0<1=\ell(b)$, and $$P_{b,w}(q)=P_{\mathrm{id},2413}(q)+q\,P_{b,2413}(q)-\!\!\!\sum_{\substack{b\le u\le2413\\ s_2u<u,\ \mu(u,2413)\ne0}}\!\!\!\mu(u,2413)\,q^{(4-\ell(u))/2}P_{b,u}(q).$$ By step 1.1 the interval $[b,2413]$ is $\{1324,1423,2314,2413\}$; left multiplication by $s_2$ swaps the values $2$ and $3$, turning these into $1234,1432,3214,3412$ of lengths $0,3,3,4$, so only $u=b$ has the required descent, and there $\mu(b,2413)=0$ because $\ell(2413)-\ell(b)=2$ is even by [F3]. The correction sum is therefore empty; step 2.1 gives $P_{\mathrm{id},2413}=1$ and step 1.2 gives $P_{b,2413}=1$, so $P_{b,w}=1+q$, with $\mu(b,w)=1$ and $\ell(w)-\ell(b)=3$.

**The comparison.** The polynomial $P_{b,w}(q)=1+q$ has leading coefficient $1$ (the coefficient of $q^{1}$, its degree being $1$) while its value at $q=1$ is $2$. The multiplicity theorem [F1] computes the ordinary Verma-flag multiplicity as $(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(b\cdot\lambda))=P_{b,w}(1)=2$, with $0$ dominant regular integral in $\mathfrak{sl}_4$ (indeed $\langle\rho,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle=1\ne0$ for every simple root and $0$ is integral). Hence the leading coefficient $1$ of the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial differs from the multiplicity $2$: the refuted claim's coefficientwise clause is false, and no selection of coefficients of $P_{b,w}$ can reproduce the multiplicity, only the total value at one can. This is a genuine failure of the claim and not an artefact of undefined quantities: $b\le w$, all polynomials are classical Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, and the multiplicity is that of the ordinary block $\mathcal O_0$.

**The grading clause.** The remaining structural clause of the refuted claim is not supplied by the cited results either: the multiplicity of [F1] is the ordinary (ungraded) Verma-flag multiplicity, and the projective dictionary of [F2] is the ungraded reduction $V(P(w\cdot\lambda))=\bar B_{w^{-1}}$, whose auxiliary grading lives on the polynomial lift and is not a grading of $\mathcal O_\lambda$. Thus the character identity at $q=1$ cannot establish that the block is graded or Koszul; the graded and $\mathrm{Ext}$ refinements belong to the separate Koszul-duality frontier, and the numerical failure of step 4.1 shows in addition that the coefficient-by-coefficient graded-decomposition interpretation is not available here. Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral type-$A$ block
$\mathcal O_\lambda$, for all $y,w\in W$
$$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=P_{y,w}(1),$$
with the pair ordered so that the multiplicity vanishes unless $y\le w$ in the
Bruhat order; in particular the Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture's multiplicity
statement holds for every dominant regular integral weight, with the same
combinatorial answer.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The classes $[L(\lambda)]$, and separately the classes $[M(\lambda)]$, form $\mathbb Z$-bases of $K_0(\mathcal O)$. For a fixed finite central-character label set $\Lambda=W\cdot\lambda$, the transition between its standard and simple classes is unitriangular in any linear order extending $\leq$. This remains true on a downward-closed subset of that finite poset. It is not a claim about finite downward ideals of all of $\mathfrak h^*$.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For the abelian category [[thm-category-o-is-abelian-and-extension-closed]], define $K_0(\mathcal O)$ as the free abelian group on isomorphism classes $[M]$, modulo $[B]=[A]+[C]$ for every short exact sequence $0\to A\to B\to C\to0$. A set of representatives suffices: every finitely generated $U(\mathfrak g)$-module is a quotient of some $U(\mathfrak g)^n$, and those quotients form a set up to isomorphism.

Define the formal character by $\operatorname{ch}M=\sum_\mu(\dim M_\mu)e^\mu$. By [[prop-equivalent-support-description-of-category-o]], its integer coefficients are finite and supported in finitely many downward cones. Let $\mathscr R$ be the group of all such integer coefficient families, with pointwise addition. It is a ring with $e^\mu e^\nu=e^{\mu+\nu}$: at a fixed resulting weight, in any pair of cones the equation $\beta+\gamma=\eta$ with $\beta,\gamma\in Q^+$ has finitely many solutions, since every simple-root coefficient is bounded. Taking weight spaces is exact, so character gives a well-defined homomorphism $K_0(\mathcal O)\to\mathscr R$. The zero object's class and character are zero.

For $x,w\in S_n$ set $$q'_{x,w}:=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^m\sum_{x=z_0<z_1<\cdots<z_m=w}p_{z_0,z_1}p_{z_1,z_2}\cdots p_{z_{m-1},z_m}\in A,$$ where the inner sum is over strictly increasing Bruhat chains from $x$ to $w$, the $m=0$ chain occurs only when $x=w$, and $p_{u,v}$ are the coefficients of the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis ([[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]). Every chain lies in a finite Bruhat interval by [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]], so the sum is finite. If $x\not\le w$ there are no chains; if $x=w$, the empty chain gives $q'_{w,w}=1$. If $x<w$, each chain has at least one factor $p_{u,v}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ with $u<v$, so $q'_{x,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$.

Let $P=(p_{x,w})$ and $Q'=(q'_{x,w})$. The matrix $N:=P-I$ is strictly triangular on the finite Bruhat poset, hence nilpotent; the $(x,w)$ entry of $N^m$ is the sum of products over chains of $m$ strict steps. Therefore $$Q'=I-N+N^2-\cdots+(-1)^M N^M=(I+N)^{-1}=P^{-1},$$ where $M$ can be any integer at least the maximum strict-chain length. In particular, $Q'P=PQ'=I$ and $$\sum_zq'_{x,z}p_{z,w}=\delta_{x,w}=\sum_zp_{x,z}q'_{z,w}.$$

The **inverse Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials** in the classical sign convention are $q_{x,w}:=\mathrm{sgn}(x)\mathrm{sgn}(w)q'_{x,w}$. If $\Sigma$ is the diagonal matrix with entries $\Sigma_{x,x}=\mathrm{sgn}(x)$, then $Q=(q_{x,w})=\Sigma Q'\Sigma$. Equivalently, if $D_x$ is the basis of $H^*=\mathrm{Hom}_A(H,A)$ dual to the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis, then $$q'_{x,w}=D_x(H_w),$$ since $H_w=\sum_zq'_{z,w}\underline H_z$.

Let $P=(p_{x,w})$, $Q'=(q'_{x,w})$ and $R=(r_{x,y})$ be the triangular matrices of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]], [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]] and [[thm-r-polynomial-recursion-and-degree-bounds]]. Then (a) $P=R\bar P$, $\bar P=\bar RP$, and $R\bar R=\bar RR=1$; (b) $Q'P=PQ'=1$, and the inversion formulas $$\overline{q'_{x,w}}=\sum_{x\le z\le w}q'_{x,z}r_{z,w},\qquad \overline{q_{x,w}}=\sum_{x\le z\le w}q_{x,z}\overline{r_{z,w}}$$ hold, i.e. $\bar Q'=Q'R$ and $\bar Q=Q\bar R$; (c) for the dual basis $D_x(\underline H_w)=\delta_{x,w}$ from [[def-inverse-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials]], $D_x(H_w)=q'_{x,w}$. The inversion is proved from the bar-duality relations alone (no finite case check).

Identify $\mathbb Z[q]$ with $\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$ by $q\mapsto v^{-2}$. For $y\le w$ in $S_n$, put $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ and define the **Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial** $P_{y,w}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q]$ by $$P_{y,w}(v^{-2})=v^{-d}p_{y,w},$$ where $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ is the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]. The parity clause of that theorem makes the right side a polynomial in $v^{-2}$. The conventions are: $P_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, $P_{w,w}=1$, $P_{y,w}$ has constant term 1, and for $y<w$ its degree is at most $(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)/2$. The **$\mu$-coefficient** is $$\mu(y,w):=	ext{coefficient of }q^{(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)/2}	ext{ in }P_{y,w},$$ defined to be 0 when $\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ is even; equivalently $\mu(y,w)$ is the coefficient of $v$ in $p_{y,w}$. One writes $\mu(y|w)
e0$ when $y
e w$ and ($y<w$ and $\mu(y,w)
e0$) or ($w<y$ and $\mu(w,y)
e0$). The dictionary with the literature is recorded for use: with the classical parameter $T_s^2=(q-1)T_s+q$ one has $H_w=v^{\ell(w)}T_w$, the element $\underline H_w$ is the basis element $C'_w$ of [EW], and $h_{y,w}=p_{y,w}$ with $v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(v^{-2})=h_{y,w}$ [EW, Remark 3.2].

Let $\le$ be the rank-inequality order on the zero-based $S_n$ of [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]], and identify it with the one-based realization by shifting inputs and values by $1$. (a) This order is the strong Bruhat order of type A: the transitive closure of covers $x\to tx$ where $t$ is a transposition and $\ell(tx)=\ell(x)+1$. (b) If $y\le w$ then $\ell(y)\le\ell(w)$, with equality iff $y=w$; every saturated chain has $\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ steps; and $y\le w$ iff $y^{-1}\le w^{-1}$. (c) $y\le w$ iff for every reduced expression $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$, $y$ is a reduced subword. (d) For every simple reflection $s$, if $y\le w$ and $\ell(sy)>\ell(y)$, then $y\le sw$; if $y\le w$ and $\ell(sw)<\ell(w)$, then $sy\le w$. (e) Every interval $[y,w]$ is finite; if $y\le w$, then $[y,w]=\{y\}\cup\bigcup_{y\to a\le w}[a,w]$.

Let $s=s_i$ be a simple reflection, $w\in S_n$ with $sw<w$, and $y\le w$. With $P_{x,z}:=0$ whenever $x\not\le z$, $$P_{y,w}(q)=q^{1-c}P_{sy,sw}(q)+q^{c}P_{y,sw}(q)-\!\!\!\sum_{\substack{y\le z\le sw\\ sz<z,\ \mu(z,sw)\ne0}}\!\!\!\mu(z,sw)\,q^{(\ell(w)-\ell(z))/2}P_{y,z}(q),$$ where $c=1$ if $sy<y$ and $c=0$ if $sy>y$; here $\mu$ is the coefficient defined in [[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]] (so the summand only occurs for $\ell(sw)-\ell(z)$ odd, and $(\ell(w)-\ell(z))/2$ is then an integer). The same recursion holds with $s\in R(w)$ (right descents) after replacing each index $x$ by $x^{-1}$, using $P_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=P_{y,w}$ and $\mu(y^{-1},w^{-1})=\mu(y,w)$.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ of type
$A_{n-1}$ with Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system $\Phi^+$, Weyl vector
$\rho$, Weyl group $W$ (identified with $S_n$) and dot action
$w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$. Fix a dominant regular integral weight
$\lambda$, i.e. $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\neq0$ for every root and
$\lambda$ integral, and let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be the corresponding regular
integral block in the conventions of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]: standard
objects $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)=M(w\cdot\lambda)$, simples $L(w\cdot\lambda)$,
indecomposable projectives $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\in W$, with
$\lambda=e\cdot\lambda$ the unique dominant and $w_0\cdot\lambda$ the unique
antidominant element and $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$.

This item freezes the following conventions, each inherited from the cited
suppliers and used verbatim below.

(i) **Multiplicity conventions.** $(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))$ is
the Verma-flag multiplicity of [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] and
$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$ the composition multiplicity, and
$$(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$$
by BGG reciprocity ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]).

(ii) **Bruhat reversal convention.** Along the bijection
$W\ni w\mapsto w\cdot\lambda$ the Bruhat order runs opposite to the dominance
order, in the two exact senses used on this page: $y\le w$ implies
$w\cdot\lambda\le y\cdot\lambda$ in the dominance order, and every nonzero
multiplicity forces the index direction, i.e.
$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]\neq0$ implies $y\le w$ in the Bruhat
order. The first sense is the inclusion direction of
[[lem-dominant-integral-dot-translates-embed-in-the-verma-module]] (for
$w\ge y$ one has $M(w\cdot\lambda)\subseteq M(y\cdot\lambda)$, so the highest
weight of the submodule is the lower one), and the second is
[[lem-jordan-holder-factors-of-verma-modules-lie-above-the-head]], which
confines every composition factor of $M(y\cdot\lambda)$ to labels
$w\ge y$. The full statement that the two orders are isomorphic as posets is
not needed here and is not asserted; only these two directions, together with
the finiteness of intervals of the Bruhat order
([[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]), are used.

(iii) **Hecke and Kazhdan–Lusztig normalization.** The Kazhdan–Lusztig basis
$\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ of the normalized type-$A$ Hecke
algebra ([[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]), with
$$p_{y,w}=v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(v^{-2})$$
in the classical $q=v^{-2}$ normalization
([[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]), support
$p_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, diagonal $p_{w,w}=1$, and simultaneous inversion
symmetry $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$.

(iv) **Soergel label and character dictionary.** Write $R_x$ for the
polynomial standard graph bimodule supported at $x$, and $B_x$ for the
normalized indecomposable polynomial Soergel bimodule, which is generally not a
standard graph bimodule. With right reduction $\bar B=B\otimes_S\mathbb C$
and left coinvariant-module values of $V$, the projective dictionary is
$$V(P(w\cdot\lambda))\cong\bar B_{w^{-1}}$$
([[thm-indecomposable-projectives-correspond-to-indecomposable-soergel-modules]]).
The graph label $x$ corresponds to the standard
$\Delta(x^{-1}\cdot\lambda)$. The individual support ranks are measured on the
polynomial lift before reduction, as in
[[prop-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-standard-filtration-ranks-under-v]];
no separated graph-support filtration of the reduced module is asserted.

For degree bookkeeping use precisely the standard-generator normalization of
[[def-type-a-standard-graph-bimodules-support-filtrations-and-character]]:
$\Delta_x(d)=R_x(d-\ell(x))$, and $r_{x,d}(B)$ counts these normalized polynomial
standard layers. Thus the coefficient polynomial is
$$m_x(B;v):=\sum_d r_{x,d}(B)v^d,\qquad h_\Delta(B)=\sum_xm_x(B;v)\widetilde T_x,\qquad\widetilde T_x=v^{\ell(x)}T_x.$$
Here $\widetilde T_x$ is the normalized **standard** Hecke element $H_x$ used
in clause (iii) and
[[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]]. The published
Soergel split-Grothendieck-ring convention instead names its simple
Kazhdan--Lusztig generators $H_i=v(T_i+1)=\widetilde T_{s_i}+v$; these must not
be confused with the standard element $H_{s_i}=vT_i$
([[thm-split-grothendieck-group-of-the-soergel-category-is-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]]).
The standard-character supplier
[[lem-the-type-a-standard-character-is-multiplicative]] identifies $h_\Delta$
with that split-Grothendieck-ring isomorphism. This records the coefficient
normalization, and does not infer the image of a general indecomposable $B_x$
by multiplying simple generators. In particular the character theorem must be
used to identify $h_\Delta(B_x)$ with $\underline H_x$; a product of simple
Soergel classes is a Bott--Samelson class and need not be $[B_x]$.
The inverse labels and all rank comparisons above use auxiliary polynomial
gradings only; forgetting them gives the ordinary projective dictionary.

derivations.claim: By [F1] the class of every standard in $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ expands in the simple basis as $[M(y\cdot\lambda)]=\sum_w[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]\,[L(w\cdot\lambda)]=\sum_wA_{y,w}[L(w\cdot\lambda)]$, where $A_{y,w}=P_{y,w}(1)$; by [F4] and [F7] the matrix $A$ is unitriangular for the Bruhat order: $A_{w,w}=1$ and $A_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$.

The matrix $A$ is the specialization at $v=1$ of the Kazhdan–Lusztig coefficient matrix $P=(p_{x,w})$, because $p_{y,w}(1)=P_{y,w}(1)$ by [F4]; specialisation $v\mapsto1$ is a ring homomorphism $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to\mathbb Z$, so the inverse matrix of $A$ is $A^{-1}=Q'(1)=(q'_{x,w}(1))$ by the two-sided inverse statement $Q'=P^{-1}$ of [F3]. By the support clause of [F3], $q'_{w,x}(1)=0$ unless $w\le x$, and all entries are integers; in particular the sum in the formula is supported on $x\ge w$, and every coefficient $q'_{w,x}(1)$ is the value at one of an integer Laurent polynomial.

The specialization is not the Möbius function in general; the following finite witness is computed inside $S_4$ with the recursion [F6]. Put $b:=1324=s_2$ and $T:=3412=s_2s_1s_3s_2$; the reduced subwords of this reduced word for $T$ give the interval $[b,T]=\{1324;\ 1342,1423,2314,3124;\ 1432,2413,3142,3214;\ 3412\}$, ten elements, and all comparable pairs of gap at most two have $P=1$ by the degree bound of [F4], so the only pair that can be nonconstant is the endpoint $(b,T)$, of gap $3$. Apply [F6] with the left descent $s=s_2$ of $T$: $s_2T=2413$, $s_2b=1234$ and $c=1$, so $P_{b,T}=P_{1234,2413}+qP_{b,2413}-\sum_z\mu(z,2413)q^{(4-\ell(z))/2}P_{b,z}$, where $z$ runs over the elements of $[b,2413]=\{1324,1423,2314,2413\}$ with $s_2z<z$; left multiplication by $s_2$ swaps the values $2$ and $3$, turning these four elements into $1234,1432,3214,3412$ of lengths $0,3,3,4$, so only $z=b$ has the required descent, and there $\mu(b,2413)=0$ because the gap $2$ is even by [F4]. Hence the correction sum vanishes, and with $P_{b,2413}=1$ (gap $2$) the recursion reduces to $P_{b,T}=P_{1234,2413}+q$. For the remaining value apply [F6] at $(1234,2413)$ with the left descent $s_1$: $s_12413=1423$ and $c=0$, so $P_{1234,2413}=qP_{2134,1423}+P_{1234,1423}-\sum_{z}\mu(z,1423)q^{(3-\ell(z))/2}P_{1234,z}$; the first term vanishes because $1423=s_3s_2$ has no reduced subword $s_1$, so $2134\not\le1423$ and $P_{2134,1423}=0$ by [F4] and [F5], and the correction sum is empty because the four elements of $[1234,1423]=\{1234,1324,1243,1423\}$ all have lengths $0,1,1,2$ raised to $1,2,2,3$ by left multiplication with $s_1$, so none is a left descent. In the signed normalization $q_{x,w}=\mathrm{sgn}(x)\mathrm{sgn}(w)q'_{x,w}$ of [F3], substituting $q'_{w,x}(1)=(-1)^{\ell(w)+\ell(x)}q_{w,x}(1)$ and using that $\ell(w)+\ell(x)$ and $\ell(w)-\ell(x)$ differ by the even number $2\ell(x)$ gives the signed inverse-Kazhdan–Lusztig sum $\mathrm{ch}\,L(w\cdot\lambda)=\sum_{x\ge w}(-1)^{\ell(w)-\ell(x)}q_{w,x}(1)\,\mathrm{ch}\,M(x\cdot\lambda)$.

The chain formula of [F3] expresses the inverse coefficients of step 2.1 as the weighted incidence-algebra inverse of $A$: $q'_{x,w}(1)=\sum_{m\ge0}(-1)^m\sum_{x=z_0<z_1<\cdots<z_m=w}P_{z_0,z_1}(1)\cdots P_{z_{m-1},z_m}(1)$, a finite sum over the strictly increasing chains of the finite interval $[x,w]$ described in [F5]. If every comparable-pair value $P_{y,z}(1)$ in $[x,w]$ equals $1$, each product in the $m$-th term equals $1$ and the alternating chain count $\sum_m(-1)^m\#\{\text{strictly increasing chains }x=z_0<\cdots<z_m=w\}$ is exactly the ordinary Bruhat Möbius value $\mu(x,w)$; so on intervals with all comparable-pair values equal to $1$ the coefficients are ordinary Bruhat Möbius numbers.

Let $n\ge1$ and $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$. For $n\ge2$, define the **normalized type-A Hecke algebra** $H_v(n)$ to be the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators $H_{s_1},\ldots,H_{s_{n-1}}$ with relations
$$H_{s_i}^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)H_{s_i},\qquad H_{s_i}H_{s_{i+1}}H_{s_i}=H_{s_{i+1}}H_{s_i}H_{s_{i+1}},\qquad H_{s_i}H_{s_j}=H_{s_j}H_{s_i}\quad(|i-j|>1).$$
For $n=1$, set $H_v(1):=A$.

Here $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$, $s_i=(i\ i+1)$, and $\ell$ is inversion length as in [[def-symmetric-group]] and [[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]. For $w\in S_n$, let $T_w$ be the standard basis element of the generic Hecke algebra of [[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]], formed from any reduced expression of $w$, and after the coefficient specialization $q\mapsto v^{-2}$ put $H_w:=v^{\ell(w)}T_w$. Equivalently, $H_w=H_{s_{i_1}}\cdots H_{s_{i_k}}$ for a reduced expression $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$. The standard-basis theorem [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] and rescaling by units show that $\{H_w:w\in S_n\}$ is an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$.

Right multiplication by a generator is
$$H_wH_{s_i}=H_{ws_i}\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)+1,\qquad H_wH_{s_i}=H_{ws_i}+(v^{-1}-v)H_w\quad\text{if }\ell(ws_i)=\ell(w)-1.$$

**Dictionary with the generic normalization.** If the generic parameter in [[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] is denoted by $q$, its relation is $T_i^2=(q-1)T_i+q$. The coefficient map $q\mapsto v^{-2}$ is the stated specialization, and $H_{s_i}=vT_i$. This gives $H_{s_i}^2=1+(v^{-1}-v)H_{s_i}$; the braid and commutation relations are unchanged. The two multiplication cases above are the standard-basis rule after the same rescaling.

**Bar assignment.** Let $F$ be the free associative $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$-algebra on the generator symbols. Define the semilinear algebra map $\iota_0:F\to F$ by $\iota_0(v)=v^{-1}$ and $\iota_0(H_{s_i})=H_{s_i}-(v^{-1}-v)$. In the quotient $H_v(n)$, the quadratic relation makes this latter element the two-sided inverse $H_{s_i}^{-1}$. The next lemma proves that $\iota_0$ preserves the defining ideal and descends to a well-defined involution $\iota$ on $H_v(n)$.

All items on this page use this normalization. It agrees with Elias–Williamson §3.2 under $H_x=v^{\ell(x)}T_x$ and $q=v^{-2}$.

In $H_v(n)$ there is a unique $A$-semilinear unital ring involution, denoted by a bar, with $\bar v=v^{-1}$ and $\overline{H_{s_i}}=H_{s_i}^{-1}$. It is multiplicative and satisfies $\overline{\overline{H_w}}=H_w$ and $\overline{H_w}=H_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$ for every $w\in S_n$; consequently each $H_w$ is invertible and $\overline{H_{w^{-1}}}=H_w^{-1}$.

For each $w\in S_n$ there is a unique element $\underline H_w\in H_v(n)$ with (i) $\overline{\underline H_w}=\underline H_w$ and (ii) $\underline H_w\in H_w+\sum_{y<w}v\mathbb Z[v]\,H_y$ (the sum over the lower Bruhat ideal of $w$). The elements $\{\underline H_w\}_{w\in S_n}$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, and writing $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ one has $p_{w,w}=1$, $p_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, $p_{y,w}\in v\mathbb Z[v]$ for $y<w$, the bar-duality $p_{x,w}=\sum_{y}r_{x,y}\,\overline{p_{y,w}}$ (matrix form $P=R\bar P$), and the symmetry $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$. Moreover for $y<w$, with $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$: $p_{y,w}=v^{d}+\text{terms of strictly smaller degree}$ and $p_{y,w}\in v^{d}\,\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$; in particular every $\underline H_w$ has integer nonnegative coefficients in the standard basis with $p_{y,w}$ of fixed parity $d\bmod 2$.

Identify $\mathbb Z[q]$ with $\mathbb Z[v^{-2}]$ by $q\mapsto v^{-2}$. For $y\le w$ in $S_n$, put $d=\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ and define the **Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial** $P_{y,w}(q)\in\mathbb Z[q]$ by $$P_{y,w}(v^{-2})=v^{-d}p_{y,w},$$ where $\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ is the Kazhdan–Lusztig basis of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]. The parity clause of that theorem makes the right side a polynomial in $v^{-2}$. The conventions are: $P_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, $P_{w,w}=1$, $P_{y,w}$ has constant term 1, and for $y<w$ its degree is at most $(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)/2$. The **$\mu$-coefficient** is $$\mu(y,w):=	ext{coefficient of }q^{(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)/2}	ext{ in }P_{y,w},$$ defined to be 0 when $\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ is even; equivalently $\mu(y,w)$ is the coefficient of $v$ in $p_{y,w}$. One writes $\mu(y|w)
e0$ when $y

e0$). The dictionary with the literature is recorded for use: with the classical parameter $T_s^2=(q-1)T_s+q$ one has $H_w=v^{\ell(w)}T_w$, the element $\underline H_w$ is the basis element $C'_w$ of [EW], and $h_{y,w}=p_{y,w}$ with $v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(v^{-2})=h_{y,w}$ [EW, Remark 3.2].

Let $\le$ be the rank-inequality order on the zero-based $S_n$ of [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]], and identify it with the one-based realization by shifting inputs and values by $1$. (a) This order is the strong Bruhat order of type A: the transitive closure of covers $x\to tx$ where $t$ is a transposition and $\ell(tx)=\ell(x)+1$. (b) If $y\le w$ then $\ell(y)\le\ell(w)$, with equality iff $y=w$; every saturated chain has $\ell(w)-\ell(y)$ steps; and $y\le w$ iff $y^{-1}\le w^{-1}$. (c) $y\le w$ iff for every reduced expression $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_k}$, $y$ is a reduced subword. (d) For every simple reflection $s$, if $y\le w$ and $\ell(sy)>\ell(y)$, then $y\le sw$; if $y\le w$ and $\ell(sw)<\ell(w)$, then $sy\le w$. (e) Every interval $[y,w]$ is finite; if $y\le w$, then $[y,w]=\{y\}\cup\bigcup_{y\to a\le w}[a,w]$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral type-$A$ block
$\mathcal O_\lambda$, for all $y,w\in W$
$$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=P_{y,w}(1),$$
with the pair ordered so that the multiplicity vanishes unless $y\le w$ in the
Bruhat order; in particular the Kazhdan–Lusztig conjecture's multiplicity
statement holds for every dominant regular integral weight, with the same
combinatorial answer.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For all weights
$\lambda$ and $\mu$,
$$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[M(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
where $P(\lambda)$ is the projective cover of $L(\lambda)$, the left-hand
multiplicity is the Verma-flag multiplicity of
[[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], and the right-hand
multiplicity is the simple composition multiplicity of the Verma module
$M(\mu)$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]).

For $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$, the **Verma module** is the induced
$\mathfrak g$-module

$$M(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}\mathbb C_\lambda,$$

where $U(\mathfrak g)$ is the quotient algebra of
[[def-universal-enveloping-algebra-as-a-tensor-quotient]] and
$\mathbb C_\lambda$ is [[def-one-dimensional-borel-module-of-weight-lambda]].
Write $v_\lambda:=1\otimes c_\lambda$.  Thus $M(\lambda)$ is the quotient of
$U(\mathfrak g)$ by the left ideal generated by $x$ for $x\in\mathfrak n^+$
and $h-\lambda(h)$ for $h\in\mathfrak h$; in particular,
$\mathfrak n^+v_\lambda=0$ and $hv_\lambda=\lambda(h)v_\lambda$.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ of type
$A_{n-1}$ with Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system $\Phi^+$, Weyl vector
$\rho$, Weyl group $W$ (identified with $S_n$) and dot action
$w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$. Fix a dominant regular integral weight
$\lambda$, i.e. $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\neq0$ for every root and
$\lambda$ integral, and let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be the corresponding regular
integral block in the conventions of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]: standard
objects $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)=M(w\cdot\lambda)$, simples $L(w\cdot\lambda)$,
indecomposable projectives $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\in W$, with
$\lambda=e\cdot\lambda$ the unique dominant and $w_0\cdot\lambda$ the unique
antidominant element and $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$.

This item freezes the following conventions, each inherited from the cited
suppliers and used verbatim below.

(i) **Multiplicity conventions.** $(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))$ is
the Verma-flag multiplicity of [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] and
$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$ the composition multiplicity, and
$$(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]$$
by BGG reciprocity ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]).

(ii) **Bruhat reversal convention.** Along the bijection
$W\ni w\mapsto w\cdot\lambda$ the Bruhat order runs opposite to the dominance
order, in the two exact senses used on this page: $y\le w$ implies
$w\cdot\lambda\le y\cdot\lambda$ in the dominance order, and every nonzero
multiplicity forces the index direction, i.e.
$[M(y\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]\neq0$ implies $y\le w$ in the Bruhat
order. The first sense is the inclusion direction of
[[lem-dominant-integral-dot-translates-embed-in-the-verma-module]] (for
$w\ge y$ one has $M(w\cdot\lambda)\subseteq M(y\cdot\lambda)$, so the highest
weight of the submodule is the lower one), and the second is
[[lem-jordan-holder-factors-of-verma-modules-lie-above-the-head]], which
confines every composition factor of $M(y\cdot\lambda)$ to labels
$w\ge y$. The full statement that the two orders are isomorphic as posets is
not needed here and is not asserted; only these two directions, together with
the finiteness of intervals of the Bruhat order
([[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]), are used.

(iii) **Hecke and Kazhdan–Lusztig normalization.** The Kazhdan–Lusztig basis
$\underline H_w=\sum_{y\le w}p_{y,w}H_y$ of the normalized type-$A$ Hecke
algebra ([[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]), with
$$p_{y,w}=v^{\ell(w)-\ell(y)}P_{y,w}(v^{-2})$$
in the classical $q=v^{-2}$ normalization
([[def-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-in-the-classical-q-normalization]]), support
$p_{y,w}=0$ unless $y\le w$, diagonal $p_{w,w}=1$, and simultaneous inversion
symmetry $p_{y^{-1},w^{-1}}=p_{y,w}$.

(iv) **Soergel label and character dictionary.** Write $R_x$ for the
polynomial standard graph bimodule supported at $x$, and $B_x$ for the
normalized indecomposable polynomial Soergel bimodule, which is generally not a
standard graph bimodule. With right reduction $\bar B=B\otimes_S\mathbb C$
and left coinvariant-module values of $V$, the projective dictionary is
$$V(P(w\cdot\lambda))\cong\bar B_{w^{-1}}$$
([[thm-indecomposable-projectives-correspond-to-indecomposable-soergel-modules]]).
The graph label $x$ corresponds to the standard
$\Delta(x^{-1}\cdot\lambda)$. The individual support ranks are measured on the
polynomial lift before reduction, as in
[[prop-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-standard-filtration-ranks-under-v]];
no separated graph-support filtration of the reduced module is asserted.

For degree bookkeeping use precisely the standard-generator normalization of
[[def-type-a-standard-graph-bimodules-support-filtrations-and-character]]:
$\Delta_x(d)=R_x(d-\ell(x))$, and $r_{x,d}(B)$ counts these normalized polynomial
standard layers. Thus the coefficient polynomial is
$$m_x(B;v):=\sum_d r_{x,d}(B)v^d,\qquad h_\Delta(B)=\sum_xm_x(B;v)\widetilde T_x,\qquad\widetilde T_x=v^{\ell(x)}T_x.$$
Here $\widetilde T_x$ is the normalized **standard** Hecke element $H_x$ used
in clause (iii) and
[[def-normalized-type-a-hecke-algebra-and-its-bar-involution]]. The published
Soergel split-Grothendieck-ring convention instead names its simple
Kazhdan--Lusztig generators $H_i=v(T_i+1)=\widetilde T_{s_i}+v$; these must not
be confused with the standard element $H_{s_i}=vT_i$
([[thm-split-grothendieck-group-of-the-soergel-category-is-the-type-a-hecke-algebra]]).
The standard-character supplier
[[lem-the-type-a-standard-character-is-multiplicative]] identifies $h_\Delta$
with that split-Grothendieck-ring isomorphism. This records the coefficient
normalization, and does not infer the image of a general indecomposable $B_x$
by multiplying simple generators. In particular the character theorem must be
used to identify $h_\Delta(B_x)$ with $\underline H_x$; a product of simple
Soergel classes is a Bott--Samelson class and need not be $[B_x]$.
The inverse labels and all rank comparisons above use auxiliary polynomial
gradings only; forgetting them gives the ordinary projective dictionary.

$\mathcal O$ with the conventions of the preceding definitions. For a weight
$\lambda$ write $\chi_\lambda$ for the generalized central character obtained
from $\lambda$, so that $\chi_\lambda=\chi_\mu$ if and only if
$\mu\in W\mathbin\cdot\lambda$
([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]), and let
